content.text:
Syncthing is overwriting the image manifest with one built on another machine.

**What's happening**

- The server learns which dev images to push to the pool from `.tmp/discobox-dev-images.json`. The image watcher writes that file, then writes `.env` (`internal/cmd/discobox-docker-image-watch/main.go:669-677`).
- Your Syncthing ignores `*/.env` but not `.tmp/`. The `/src/*/tmp` rule in `~/src/../.stignore` doesn't match the dotted `.tmp`. So the manifest syncs between machines and `.env` doesn't.
- Your checkout shows this directly:
  - `.env` was written at 22:06:34 and names `claude-code:dev-510a0d4f9d75`, which exists locally.
  - The manifest is newer, written at 22:07:33, and names `claude-code:dev-07cc2d216e5f` and `pool-agent:dev-06b55555eb53`. Neither image exists on this daemon. Your local watcher doesn't write the manifest after `.env`, so that one came from another machine.
  - `.tmp/` holds 10 `discobox-dev-images.sync-conflict-*.json` files from two other Syncthing devices. This has been happening since at least 2026-09-24.
- `discobox-server` restarted at 23:13 and read the other machine's manifest. `DevelopmentImageSynchronizer.ensure` then finds the image missing on the pool daemon and tries to copy it from your local daemon. It isn't there either, so it fails at `server/providers/dockerworker/image_sync.go:191`.

**Why it never recovers**

The watcher's self-heal only checks whether the images it built still exist locally (`missingImageSpecs`). They all do, so it never rebuilds and never rewrites the manifest. Nothing else corrects a manifest that was replaced underneath it. The pool reconcile just retries the same error, which is why you're at attempt 641.

**Fix**

1. Add `/src/*/.tmp` to the `.stignore` that already has `/src/*/tmp`. Do the same on the other machines, or each one will keep replacing the others' manifests.
2. Restart `task dev`. The watcher marks every image pending at startup, so it rewrites the manifest from your local images and the server picks it up. If you'd rather not restart, touching any watched input rebuilds that image, but a full restart is the surer reset.
3. Delete the `.tmp/*.sync-conflict-*.json` files. They're inert, just clutter.

A more robust fix would be for the watcher to check that the manifest on disk is the one it last wrote. That only matters if `.tmp` can be changed outside the watcher, which is only the case here because of Syncthing, so the ignore rule is the right fix. I haven't changed any code or config.

content.text:
I added `*/.tmp` to `~/src/stignore`, right after `*/.env`. `~/src/.stignore` is already a symlink to that file, so nothing else needed changing.

The rule only applies on machines that load it. If `stignore` is synced to your other machines and they have the same symlink, they'll pick it up. Otherwise add the line there too, or they'll keep sending their manifests.

The bad manifest that's already in your checkout stays. Restart `task dev` to rewrite it from your local images, and you can delete the `.tmp/*.sync-conflict-*.json` files.
